cover.title: Timescale Cloud
cover.categories: Product Design, UI Design, Design System

header: Timescale Cloud is a database as a service. Developers get a powerful relational database without having to set up or manage the infrastructure under it. I led the design, from the first setup steps to the dashboards developers check every day.
seo_description: Product design case study: designing Timescale Cloud, a database as a service, to be clear, fast to set up, and built for developers.

layout.title: The challenge
text: Developers can run Postgres almost anywhere. To win them over, Timescale Cloud had to be a database service they actually want to use: the easiest place to get started, and the clearest place to see what’s going on.

layout.title: Everything in one place
text: Developers shouldn’t have to dig for the basics. Each database gets one overview page that shows how healthy it is, what specs it’s running on, and what it costs.
Any change to the database starts from this page, so nobody has to go looking.

layout.title: From empty to running
text: The first few minutes with a new database matter most. The Actions page turns setup into a short list, grouped by what you’re trying to do, like speeding up queries or getting ready for production.
Each task shows how long it takes, so it’s easy to pick one and finish it.

layout.title: Pricing in plain sight
text: Nobody likes a surprise bill. Plans sit side by side with the same rows, so it’s easy to compare compute, high availability, and backups, and see what an upgrade gets you.

layout.title: No DBA hat required
text: Once a database is running, developers want to know it’s healthy. Monitoring puts CPU, memory, queries, and storage on one screen.
The result is a clean, modern interface built for developers, not database admins. They can check on a database at a glance and get back to building.
